checks: With positive sampled mass and at least two sites, equality and the strictly positive variation coefficient force every sampled weight to equal W>0.

Brunn–Minkowski gives at least W between extreme sampled bases and concavity gives continuity in the interior. Equality of volumes forces the section volume to be constant on the open interval. Any additional point at an outside base together with the nearest full extreme fiber yields positive extra volume.

The two actual endpoint fibers have positive equal volume, and their Minkowski midpoint has no volume slack. The Brunn–Minkowski equality case forces translates. Their actual interpolants are contained in the sections and have the same positive volume, hence equal them, proving the shear formula.

The converse integrates the shear product directly. In the single-sample case any extra base point gives a positive-volume cone; in the zero-mass case the right-hand side is zero by definition. The statement agrees with source d46094c158197e98 §3.
